class.name: SingleSurfaceMeshND
class.brief_description: Base class for ND meshes with a single surface.
class.description: SingleSurfaceMeshND is the base class for all ND meshes with a single surface. Meshes are used to represent the visuals of objects in ND space. All single-surface ND meshes have vertices, and either have edges or can have edges computed. For a wireframe-only mesh, use [WireMeshND] or one of its descendants. Meshes may also have simplex cells, which are the equivalent of triangles in 3D meshes. For a simplex cell mesh, use [CellMeshND] or one of its descendants. Advanced users can create custom mesh classes by extending the appropriate class.

method.name: _get_edge_indices
method.description: Callback method that should return the edge indices of a mesh. Do not call this method. This can be overridden by derived classes when creating a custom mesh type in GDScript or another scripting language. See [method get_edge_indices] for details of the returned data.

method.name: _get_fallback_material
method.description: Callback method that should return a fallback [MaterialND] for the mesh. This is used when neither the [MeshInstanceND] nor the [SingleSurfaceMeshND] itself have a material defined. Do not call this method. This can be overridden by derived classes when creating a custom mesh type in GDScript or another scripting language. This is only needed when creating a completely custom [SingleSurfaceMeshND] type; built-in types such as [CellMeshND] and [WireMeshND] already define a fallback material, and overriding this function does nothing for them.

method.name: _get_normal_values
method.description: Callback method that should return the mesh's normal value pool. Do not call this method. Override this in a custom mesh class to supply values referenced by the simplex cell normal indices. See [method get_normal_values].

method.name: _get_texture_map_values
method.description: Callback method that should return the mesh's texture map value pool. Do not call this method. Override this in a custom mesh class to supply values referenced by the simplex cell texture map indices. See [method get_texture_map_values].

method.name: _get_vertex_positions
method.description: Callback method that should return the vertices of a mesh. Do not call this method. This can be overridden by derived classes when creating a custom mesh type in GDScript or another scripting language. See [method get_vertex_positions] for details of the returned data.

method.name: get_edge_indices
method.description: Gets the edge indices of the mesh. Every 2 integers defines an edge. Each integer is an index to the vertices array. Integers in this array should not exceed the length of the vertices array, or else the mesh is invalid.

method.name: get_edge_positions
method.description: Gets the edge positions of the mesh. Each VectorN ([PackedFloat64Array]) in the array is a position in meters in ND space. Edges are defined by two vertices, and the positions in this array are the positions of the vertices that make up the edges. This value is calculated from a combination of the edge indices and the vertices arrays, see [method get_edge_indices] and [method get_vertex_positions].

method.name: get_normal_values
method.description: Returns the shared normal values referenced by [method CellMeshND.get_simplex_cell_normal_indices]. Each [PackedFloat64Array] is a normal vector that should be normalized and may have at most N components, with missing trailing components treated as zero. An empty value is a zero-vector fallback for missing normal data. The array may be empty when the mesh has no normals.

method.name: get_texture_map_values
method.description: Returns the shared texture map values referenced by [method CellMeshND.get_simplex_cell_texture_map_indices]. Each [PackedFloat64Array] is a position in texture space with at most N-1 components, usually between 0.0 and 1.0 on each axis. Missing trailing components are treated as zero. An empty value is a zero-vector fallback for missing texture map data. The array may be empty when the mesh has no texture mapping.

method.name: get_vertex_positions
method.description: Gets the vertices of the mesh. Each VectorN ([PackedFloat64Array]) in the array is a vertex defined as a position in meters in ND space. Vertices are referenced by many other arrays in the mesh, such as the edge indices or cell indices. For an N-dimensional mesh, the first position has N components. Other positions may have fewer components to save memory, with missing trailing components treated as zero, but must not have more than N components.

method.name: has_edge_indices
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the mesh has an edge with the given indices. This method checks if there is an edge directly connecting the vertices with the given indices, by searching the array returned by [method get_edge_indices]. [b]Note:[/b] For efficiency, the input indices have their order normalized, so [code]has_edge_indices(2, 1)[/code] will be converted to [code]has_edge_indices(1, 2)[/code] before checking. You must ensure that your mesh has consistent edge ordering.

method.name: to_array_wire_mesh
method.description: Converts this mesh to an [ArrayWireMeshND]. The array mesh will have the same vertices, edges, material, resource name, and metadata as this mesh. The material is shared between the two meshes, but everything else is a copy. Converting to an array mesh is useful for modifying the geometry of the mesh, such as adding or removing vertices or edges.

method.name: to_wire_mesh
method.description: Converts this mesh to a [WireMeshND]. This method will use the best conversion available. If no specialized conversion is available, the method will return an [ArrayWireMeshND]. See [method to_array_wire_mesh] for more details.

members.member: The [MaterialND] used to render the mesh. This material defines the appearance of the mesh, including its color, texture, and lighting properties. The [WireMaterialND] type is intended for wireframe meshes. If no material is set, the mesh should render with default settings. The material may be overridden on a [MeshInstanceND] node by setting the [member MeshInstanceND.material_override] property.
